status: PARTIALLY FIXED — user reported the cursor pointing at the wrong thing during playback. Root-caused to two compounding bugs in lib/teacher-pointer.ts, both demonstrated with a per-word trace before changing anything. (1) normalizedWords kept trailing sentence punctuation (the character class allows '.' because a decimal point is meaningful mid-token), so the spoken word '5.' never matched the anchor label '5'. (2) Column-method anchors are labelled with single DIGITS, which repeat across cells, and a stale label match within +/-4 words outranked everything else — so for the very common step 'Write 6 and carry 5' EVERY word resolved to the same anchor and the cursor never moved to the carry cell at all. Key realisation: those anchors already carry an authored pen order (data-teacher-sequence, set from the step's cellKeys/carryKeys in ColumnMethodRenderer), which IS the teaching order — the fuzzy matcher was overriding good authored data with worse guesses. Fix: strip edge punctuation; only allow DISTINCTIVE labels (containing letters, length > 2) to win a word match; when no anchor has a distinctive label, follow the authored sequence advancing with narration progress. Word matching is preserved where it genuinely works (labelled diagrams: 'gravity', 'friction'). Verified live with Playwright on a real 2-digit x 2-digit lesson: the cursor now visits 3 distinct digit anchors in order across the step (t=5.6s, 10.3s, 13.5s) instead of pinning to one. Regression tests in __tests__/components/TeacherPointer.test.ts (monotonic pen order, punctuation, distinctive labels still matched, never points past the last anchor). suite 816/816. STILL PARTIAL — this does NOT deliver DEF-004's original ask of an explicitly authored focusTargetId per narration segment. Within a step the cursor is still distributed by narration PROGRESS across the anchors, not by an exact word-to-element mapping, so the moment it moves between anchors is approximate (in the trace above it left the '6' cell at the word 'Write' rather than after speaking '6'). topic: Addition & Subtraction -- "Column subtraction/addition of numbers with more than 4 digits" (Y5), "Add and subtract integers" (Y6)
lesson_id: cache_key v19|y5m-add-subtract|curriculum|secure|lesson|column subtraction of numbers with more than 4 digits; v19|y5m-add-subtract|...|guided|...; v19|y6m-add-subtract|curriculum|secure|guided|add and subtract integers

steps_to_reproduce: 1. POST http://localhost:3000/api/ks2-lesson with topicId=y5m-add-subtract, skill="Column subtraction of numbers with more than 4 digits", kind=lesson (or guided), force=true. 2. Read response.lesson.workedExample: question="$62,403 - 27,568$", answer="376", steps=["Set up the columns: Write 403 on top and 27 underneath to subtract.", ...], whiteboard.blocks contains a column_method block with rows ["403","-27","376"]. 3. Independently confirmed root cause: `npx tsx -e "import {buildMethodForQuestion} from './lib/methods'; console.log(buildMethodForQuestion('$62,403 - 27,568$'))"` returns builderId=column_subtraction, answer=376 -- byte-identical to the API's output, proving the deterministic builder (not the LLM) authored the wrong answer/steps/whiteboard. 4. Confirmed this happens at serve time, not just at original generation: app/api/ks2-lesson/route.ts:555-559 (inside hardenWorkedExample, called on every cache read at line 848-850) unconditionally overwrites lesson.workedExample.answer with deterministicMathsAnswer(question).answer whenever it disagrees with the model's own answer, treating the deterministic builder as ground truth. 5. Root cause of the builder's wrong answer: lib/methods/normalize-math-text.ts normalizeMathText() never strips thousands-comma separators; lib/methods/column-addition.ts parseSubtractionOperands()/parseAdditionOperands() use regex /(\d{1,6})\s*-\s*(\d{1,6})/ which only matches contiguous digit runs, so on "62,403 - 27,568" it matches the digit run immediately before " - " ("403") and the digit run immediately after ("27"), silently computing 403-27=376 instead of 62403-27568. The same unguarded \d{1,6} pattern (with no comma-stripping) exists in parseMultiplicationOperands (lib/methods/column-multiplication.ts:485-497) and the division operand parser (lib/methods/long-division.ts:224), so any comma-formatted operand >=1,000 in those question types is equally at risk, though not separately reproduced here. 6. Quantified against the live cache (437-row ks2_lesson_cache table, question/answer TEXT fields only -- no pupil data queried): of 30 cached questions matching a pure "A + B" / "A - B" pattern with at least one operand >=1,000, 4 have a stored answer that disagrees with the correct comma-aware arithmetic -- and all 4 are specifically the workedExample field (the main taught example) on the y5m-add-subtract and y6m-add-subtract lessons; every sibling tryThis/guidedPractice/independentPractice/quickCheck question on the SAME lessons, for the SAME skill, is correct. This confirms the defect is isolated to the workedExample-specific override path (route.ts:555-559), not the general answer pipeline (lib/ks2-maths-accuracy.ts's hardenKS2MathsPracticeAnswers, which already correctly excludes workedExample from its own scope and handles the other fields correctly via a different, unaffected code path).
expected_result: The worked example teaching a Year 5/6 pupil column subtraction/addition of 5-digit numbers shows the real question's numbers, correct step-by-step working, a whiteboard matching those numbers, and the correct final answer (e.g. 62,403 - 27,568 = 34,835).
actual_result: The worked example's steps, whiteboard column-method block, and final answer all silently solve a different, much simpler problem (403-27=376) than the question actually displayed above them (62,403-27,568), with no error, warning, or validation failure surfaced anywhere in the API response. This is the exact defect pattern the audit brief calls out by name: "narration to mention content absent from the board" / an architecture where a component's output is disconnected from the authored question. It is currently live in the cache serving real requests (confirmed via a direct, uncached force=true regeneration producing the identical wrong 376 answer, not a stale one-off).
evidence: app/api/ks2-lesson/route.ts:548-559 (hardenWorkedExample override) and :848-850 (applied on cache read); lib/methods/normalize-math-text.ts (full file -- no comma-stripping anywhere); lib/methods/column-addition.ts:240-249 (parseSubtractionOperands regex); lib/methods/column-multiplication.ts:485-497 and lib/methods/long-division.ts:224 (same unguarded pattern, not separately reproduced); raw API response captured via curl (POST /api/ks2-lesson, topicId=y5m-add-subtract, kind=lesson) showing question/steps/whiteboard/answer mismatch; direct call to buildMethodForQuestion() reproducing the identical 376 answer outside the API, isolating the bug to the deterministic builder; live cache sweep (ks2_lesson_cache, 437 rows, question/answer text only) quantifying 4-of-30 pure-calculation comma-formatted questions wrong, all 4 in the workedExample field specifically.
likely_root_cause: normalizeMathText() (shared by every operand parser in lib/methods/) does not strip thousands-comma separators before regex matching; the \d{1,6} operand-matching regexes therefore only see contiguous digit runs and silently truncate any comma-grouped number, producing a confidently wrong but well-formed answer with no exception thrown. app/api/ks2-lesson/route.ts then trusts this deterministic result unconditionally as "single source of truth" (its own comment, line 549-551) and overwrites the LLM's answer -- which in the observed case (tryThis: 73,205-38,467=34,738, correct) was right -- with the parser's wrong one, specifically for the workedExample field.
recommended_fix: Add comma-stripping to normalizeMathText() (e.g. strip a comma between two digits when followed by exactly 3 more digits: /(\d),(?=\d{3}\b)/g -> ''), which is the single shared entry point for every operand parser in lib/methods/ -- this fixes column addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division parsing in one place. No data migration or cache purge is needed: hardenWorkedExample() re-derives the answer on every serve (route.ts:848-850), so the fix self-heals all 437 cached rows the next time each is read. After deploying the fix, re-run the cache sweep to confirm 0-of-N wrong, and specifically re-check the 4 identified rows (cache_key values in steps_to_reproduce).
regression_test: Unit test: parseSubtractionOperands('$62,403 - 27,568$') must return {a:62403,b:27568} (and equivalent tests for +, x, and division parsers with comma-formatted operands >=1,000). Add an integration test asserting POST /api/ks2-lesson for y5m-add-subtract and y6m-add-subtract returns a workedExample.answer matching independently-computed arithmetic on the stated question, for both kind=lesson and kind=guided.
estimated_effort: Small (single shared-function fix + cache self-heals) -- Small to Medium if the multiplication/division parsers need separate confirmation and tests

For any skill not explicitly special-cased (fraction simplify/compare, rounding), the function falls through to `return tax.skill;` -- i.e. it feeds the SKILL'S OWN NAME in as the "question" (e.g. the literal string "Scale factors and scale drawings"), not a real question with real numbers. expected_result: A generated lesson whose worked example includes its coordinate-grid diagram, served to the pupil.
actual_result: ~75% of fresh generations returned HTTP 422 (missing_visual), which the client surfaces to the pupil as 'Sorry, the lesson couldn't load' after exhausting its retries. Instrumentation showed the model ALWAYS emitted a valid coordinate_graph block (on failures as well as successes) and that finish_reason was 'stop' on every call (no truncation; ~1550-1730 of 2600 allowed completion tokens; JSON.parse succeeded every time). Every failure was instead a silent parser drop: parseWorkedExampleWhiteboard required xRange/yRange on a coordinate_graph and discarded the whole block when the model omitted them, which it does on most 'read the coordinates'-style questions (it supplies correct points but no axis ranges). With every block dropped, the lesson failed the requireVisual check. A correct, usable diagram was being thrown away over two pieces of derivable metadata.
evidence: Live instrumented run (KS2_DEBUG_VISUAL=1) over 4 requests / 8 generations: every completion logged finishReason:'stop' and 'model emitted blocks: [coordinate_graph, text]'; failures logged 'DROPPED coordinate_graph: bad axis ranges { xRangeRaw: undefined, yRangeRaw: undefined }' followed by 'after normalise/fitness: { normalised: [text], survivedFitness: [] }'. likely_root_cause: app/api/ks2-lesson/route.ts parseWorkedExampleWhiteboard(): the coordinate_graph branch validated block.xRange/block.yRange and `continue`d (dropping the block) when either was missing or malformed, before extracting the points/segments from which those ranges are trivially derivable. The identical 422 shape for 'model produced nothing' vs 'parser discarded everything' is why two earlier passes mis-attributed this to LLM flakiness and attempted retry-prompt mitigations instead.
recommended_fix: Derive the missing axis ranges from the block's own points/segment endpoints rather than dropping the block, matching coordinateGraph() in lib/methods/ks2-topic-builders.ts (pad by 1; always include the origin so all four quadrants read correctly). Never override model-supplied ranges; fill only the missing axis of a partially-specified pair; keep dropping a graph that has no geometry at all rather than inventing a window.

The cuboid_array diagram was then drawn as 2x2x1, so it AGREED with the wrong answer and the internal-consistency check passed — the diagram silently contradicted the question instead of the answer. steps_to_reproduce: Serve the cached lesson (no force): POST /api/ks2-lesson with topicId=y5m-mult-div-a, skill='Multiples', kind=lesson. Observe the answers.

actual_result: Served (21x): 'Write the first five multiples of 8.' -> '8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80' (TEN, not five). 'What is the next multiple of 6 after 30?' -> '6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60' (a list, not an answer). 'Write the first four multiples of 7.' -> ten values. likely_root_cause: lib/methods/multiples-factors.ts parseMultiplesQuestion(): digit-only count capture plus a Math.max(count,5) clamp, and an over-broad fallback that claimed any text containing 'multiple'.

topic: Converting Units — metric units of length, mass and capacity
lesson_id: y5m-converting-units (guided: "convert metric units", "metric units of length, mass and capacity")
steps_to_reproduce: Call parseUnitConversion("Convert 5 m to millimetres.") — returned from="m", to="m" and an answer of "5 m" instead of 5000 mm. Also run scripts/audit-cached-answers.ts: 57 real "Convert X to Y" cached items sat in UNVERIFIABLE because spelled-out unit names were not recognised at all.
expected_result: Spelled-out and abbreviated unit names both parse to the correct unit, and metric answers are free of floating-point artefacts.
actual_result: THREE distinct problems. (1) SILENT WRONG CONVERSION: the regex alternation listed "m" before "mm"/"ml", so a spelled-out target prefix-matched the shorter abbreviation — "Convert 5 m to millimetres" parsed m->m and answered "5 m" (correct 5000 mm); "Convert 250 cm to millimetres" parsed cm->m and answered "2.5 m" (correct 2500 mm). Not a miss: a confidently wrong answer. (2) COVERAGE GAP: spelled-out names were otherwise unrecognised, leaving 57 real cached conversion questions with no deterministic check, plus the "How many X are in Y?" phrasing (target unit stated first) unsupported entirely. (3) Exposed by fixing (1) and (2): SEVEN cached items were serving answers to a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT question — "Convert 4.6 m to centimetres" answered "3/5 = 0.6 = 60%", "Convert 2.7 m to centimetres" answered "7/10 = 0.7 = 70%" (7x each) — decimal-to-fraction-to-percentage conversions attached to unit-conversion questions.
evidence: Direct probe before fix: "Convert 5 m to millimetres" -> parsed m->m, "5 m"; "Convert 250 cm to millimetres" -> cm->m, "2.5 m". scripts/audit-cached-answers.ts diff after fix: UNVERIFIABLE 962 -> 904, 51 newly verified-and-agreeing, 7 newly caught wrong answers. Live serve of both affected lessons after fix: 13 conversion answers checked against each question own numbers — 0 wrong, 0 float artefacts.
likely_root_cause: lib/methods/ks2-topic-builders.ts parseUnitConversion(): abbreviation-only alternation, ordered shortest-first, with no word boundary. Separately buildUnitConversion() used raw IEEE754 arithmetic on power-of-ten factors.
recommended_fix: Match unit tokens longest-first with word boundaries, accept spelled-out names, map every spelling to a canonical abbreviation, support the "How many X are in Y?" order, decline cross-family and no-op conversions, and round power-of-ten results with toPrecision(12) so pupil-facing text never shows 459.99999999999994 or "divide by 9.999999999999998".
regression_test: __tests__/lib/unit-conversion.test.ts — 7 cases covering the prefix-match bug, spelled-out names in both positions, the "How many X are in Y?" order, LaTeX-wrapped units and the "into" connector, float-artefact freedom in BOTH the answer and the teaching text, and cross-family/no-op declines.
